about: What Shree-Lipi's own composers write for Unicode Gujarati in the Shree-Lipi 7 Gujarati fonts (SHREE-GUJ7-*). Each row: the Unicode string, the preferred bytes (hex, one byte per glyph code: what the 7 composer types for it), and, when there are any, the other spellings the composer also accepts for the same text. Captured from S8GujU64.dll and S8Guj764.dll (Shree-Lipi nxt) by typing the same keys into both; tools/Guj7Truth builds and checks the shree-guj7 and shree-guj456 tables against it. Rows that end in a bare virama hold the composer's answer while it waits for the next letter (a half form); at the end of a word the tables write the visible halant instead. The ru and ruu rows are written as the ligatures Shree's own ru/ruu keys type, and ૰ (whose code Word draws as nothing, and which no other code of the fonts draws) is passed through as itself and reported (U+0AF0). "exceptions" says, row by row, what they write ("the table writes <hex>: why" - a U+XXXX token is that character, passed through -, or "the table leaves it out and reports it: why").
